This turns that into a rhythm, a set of repeatable plays, and the specific mechanics for each. 8 9 --- 10 11 ## 1. The mandate, consolidated 12 13 What the sessions actually assigned you: 14 15 | # | Responsibility | From | 16 |---|---|---| 17 | 1 | Own dependency discovery during refinement | M1 — the strongest expectation raised | 18 | 2 | Protect Salesforce / PWA Kit reuse; challenge "let's build this" | M1 | 19 | 3 | Own component governance — prevent duplicate Buttons, Links, utilities | M1 | 20 | 4 | Strengthen FE PR review criteria | M1 | 21 | 5 | Improve estimation accuracy — surface hidden work before planning | M1 (Jasmijn, repeatedly) | 22 | 6 | Embed accessibility in component stories, not as follow-up | M1 + M2 | 23 | 7 | Follow up design-system gaps with Kiera / design owners | M1 | 24 | 8 | Define the atoms governance model + a refinement checklist | M1 (strategic) | 25 | 9 | Component completeness — all variants designed upfront | M2 | 26 | 10 | Define a standard renderer contract between Contentful models and React components | M2 | 27 | 11 | Ensure components gracefully handle optional fields | M2 | 28 | 12 | Document accessibility expectations component-by-component | M2 | 29 | 13 | Own page-level validation — visual, responsive, integration, design parity | M2 | 30 | 14 | Push back where requirements are unclear before sizing | M2 | 31 | 15 | Support incremental assembly (build → drop in → verify) | M2 | 32 | 16 | Separate component-build effort from page-composition effort in estimates | M2 | 33 34 **The through-line, in Tim's words:** *"FED leadership needs to identify what already exists before the team commits to building something new."* 35 36 **The one to resist as stated.** #1 makes you a serial gate across both squads' refinement sessions. It won't scale and it will slip. Play 1 handles this by moving the lookup to where the story is drafted and keeping only the judgement calls for yourself. 37 38 --- 39 40 ## 2. Your operating rhythm 41 42 Sixteen responsibilities, four moments. Everything below hangs off this. 43 44 | When | Plays | Time | 45 |---|---|---| 46 | **Story drafting** (BA-initiated, async) | 1 — reuse & dependency check | Async, minutes per story | 47 | **Refinement** (per story) | 1, 3, 9, 14 — dependencies, variants, push-back | In the session | 48 | **Pre-sprint-planning** (weekly) | 2 — estimation validation | ~30 min | 49 | **PR review** (continuous) | 5 — the human-only checks | Per PR | 50 | **Design review** (weekly, with Kiera) | 6 — design-system gaps | Standing slot | 51 52 Two standing items that don't fit a cadence: the **renderer contract** (Play 4, once per Contentful component) and **page-level validation** (Play 7, once per page assembly). 53 54 --- 55 56 ## Play 1 — The reuse & dependency check 57 58 *Covers responsibilities 1, 2, 3, 8* 59 60 ### The ladder (agreed in M1) 61 62 ``` 63 Salesforce / PWA Kit capability 64 ↓ (nothing fits) 65 Existing shared component in overrides/ 66 ↓ (nothing fits) 67 Existing pattern 68 ↓ (nothing fits) 69 New implementation ← justify this out loud 70 ``` 71 72 ### Where to actually look 73 74 | Question | Source | 75 |---|---| 76 | Does a Base, Override or Custom component already exist? | `.claude/registry/components.md` — columns: **Origin · Path · Props · Tier · Squad · Consumers**. Regenerated automatically by the pre-commit hook on any `overrides/app/**` change | 77 | Same for hooks / utils / pages / routes | `.claude/registry/{hooks,utils,pages,routes}.md` | 78 | What's in the base package? | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` and `/app/hooks/` | 79 | Is it already claimed by a squad? | Registry `Squad` column · `.claude/rules/squadA.md` | 80 | What tier am I about to touch? | Registry `Tier` column, or `/audit-tier` | 81 82 The `Origin` column is doing most of the work: **`Base` means it exists but isn't scaffolded into `overrides/` yet** — which is a cost, not a free win (see below). 83 84 ### Worked examples, already verified 85 86 | Ask | What already exists | 87 |---|---| 88 | Size selector | Base `swatch-group/` — index, swatch, plus an existing test | 89 | Add to bag | Base `product-view/index.jsx` — already does `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the button and label, the add-to-cart modal, bundle handling, and an `updateCart` variant | 90 | Max purchase quantity | Base `quantity-picker/` | 91 | Variant resolution | `use-controlled-variations`, `use-derived-product`, `use-add-to-cart-modal` | 92 93 Worth knowing before SFCC-650 is sized: its description says *"Cart API integration is in scope"*, but the base already performs the cart call. That story should read as **extend `product-view`**, not build cart integration. 94 95 ### The hidden cost to name every time 96 97 If `Origin = Base`, the component isn't in `overrides/` yet, and AGENTS.md's **Copy-first rule** applies before any functional work: 98 99 1. Copy base file → mirrored path in `overrides/` 100 2. Convert to TypeScript, fix imports 101 3. `npx tsc --noEmit` 102 4. Add a temporary `console.log` marker 103 5. **Stop — a human confirms the override renders instead of the base** 104 6. Then build; remove markers 105 106 It's serialised and human-gated. **The first story against a given base component pays it; later ones don't.** This is the single most common reason a story looks small and isn't — exactly Jasmijn's concern. Either split it into an enabler story or size the first story accordingly. 107 108 ### Making this scale (the fix for #1) 109 110 Add one line to the BA prompt template in Confluence 274137093: 111 112 > *"Check `.claude/registry/components.md` — does a Base, Override or Custom component already cover this? Report Origin, Tier, Squad and Consumer count."* 113 114 That makes four of the six refinement questions self-service. You keep the two that need judgement: 115 116 - **Is extending the base the right call, or is a Zimmermann-specific build justified?** 117 - **Is the design-system prerequisite real, or can we proceed?** 118 119 ### Preventing duplicate atoms (#3, #8) 120 121 The atoms question — *"when does an atom deserve its own story?"* — is largely already answered by existing convention rather than needing a new model: 122 123 - A story is required for anything **exported from its folder** under `overrides/app/components/` or `/pages/`. 124 - **Not** required for internal sub-components that only render inside one parent — cover their variants via the parent's stories. 125 - The Storybook categorisation (`Foundation / Elements / Layout / Commerce / Forms / Pages / Contentful`) gives you the vocabulary: `Elements/` *is* the atoms layer. 126 127 Applied to 04.7's `↳ Sub-component` rows: Pause/Play, Footer Item, Footer Textfield, Icons don't each need a story unless independently reusable. Without that rule the Footer alone generates four. 128 129 --- 130 131 ## Play 2 — Estimation validation 132 133 *Covers responsibilities 5, 16* 134 135 Run this before sprint planning, not in it. 136 137 ### The re-baseline to communicate once 138 139 M2 concluded pages become assemblies. The honest consequence: 140 141 - **Homepage / page estimates should go down.** Composition genuinely is cheaper. 142 - **Component estimates should go up by more than the pages save.** 143 144 Because a component story now carries: all variants upfront + accessibility AC + a mandatory Storybook story + a test where logic-heavy + Copy-first scaffolding on first touch. 145 146 If only the first half of that lands, the programme will look like it got faster and won't have. Say this out loud in planning — once, clearly. 147 148 ### Split the two kinds of effort (#16) 149 150 | Component build | Page composition | 151 |---|---| 152 | Real frontend development | Assembly and configuration | 153 | Variants, states, accessibility | Integration testing | 154 | Storybook + tests | Visual validation | 155 | Sized as build work | Sized as validation work | 156 157 Don't let them be estimated with the same scale. 158 159 ### Challenge list 160 161 For each story before it's sized: 162 163 - [ ] `Origin = Base`? → Copy-first cost is in, or split out 164 - [ ] All variants captured, or only the ones on the first page? 165 - [ ] Accessibility written as AC, or assumed? 166 - [ ] Storybook story accounted for? 167 - [ ] Designs confirmed, or still in progress? (04.7 status column) 168 - [ ] Does it depend on anything in Play 8's open list? 169 - [ ] Composition variant hiding as a configuration variant? (Play 3) 170 171 --- 172 173 ## Play 3 — Component completeness & variant review 174 175 *Covers responsibilities 9, 11* 176 177 M2's rule: a component isn't complete until it covers all supported variants, and the page just configures it. One Editorial Card, not a Homepage one and a PLP one. 178 179 ### The distinction to hold 180 181 | Kind | Examples | How it's built | 182 |---|---|---| 183 | **Configuration variant** | text alignment, CTA on/off, title on/off, body copy present/absent | Props on one component ✅ Tim's rule applies directly | 184 | **Composition variant** | 1 vs 2 column, 3-up vs 4-up grids | A **container/slot component** — structurally a second component | 185 186 This matters because a composition variant priced as a prop will be under-estimated. On the Studio Experiences path especially, a repeating structure can't be a prop — the composition primitive is `children`. So "one Editorial Card with all variants" often resolves to *two* components: the card, plus a container holding one or two. 187 188 Better outcome — the container is reusable anywhere — but it changes the count. Catch it at refinement. 189 190 ### Why "upfront" is a hard requirement here, not a preference 191 192 The Contentful sync is **additive-only — it cannot delete a field from a published content type**. Getting the variant model wrong isn't rework, it's semi-permanent. This is the strongest argument you have for holding the line on variant completeness, and it supports Tim's position rather than fighting it. 193 194 ### Optional-field handling (#11) 195 196 M2: don't assume CMS fields are populated. Every Contentful-backed component needs AC for the absent case — no empty space, no placeholder, no layout break. Make it a standing question in refinement rather than a per-story discovery. 197 198 --- 199 200 ## Play 4 — The renderer contract 201 202 *Covers responsibility 10* 203 204 M2 asked for "a standard renderer contract between Contentful models and React components." This is the artifact that makes the Contentful story and the PWA Kit story independently workable — without it they drift, and additive-only sync makes drift expensive. 205 206 **The requirement it satisfies:** `02-contentful.md` §2 — *"TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time."* 207 208 **The artifact:** one table, identical in both stories of every Contentful pair. 209 210 | Field ID | Display name | Type / control | Required | Localised | Notes | 211 |---|---|---|---|---|---| 212 | `image` | Image | Media | Yes | No | | 213 | `imageAlt` | Image Alt Text | shortText | No | Yes | behaviour when empty — see Play 6 | 214 | `bodyCopy` | Body Copy | longText | No | Yes | | 215 | `ctaLabel` | CTA Label | shortText | No | Yes | CTA renders only if label **and** URL set | 216 | `ctaUrl` | CTA URL | shortText | No | No | internal → same tab; external → new tab + `rel="noopener noreferrer"` | 217 218 **Field IDs, not display names.** "Body copy" in prose is where drift starts. 219 220 **You own the template; the BA fills it; you sign off the field IDs before the Contentful story is built.** That signature is the cheapest possible insurance against an undeletable wrong field. 221 222 **Note for the ordering question:** for Studio Experiences components the contract is generated from the React props rather than authored first — so the review point moves to the component's prop type. Which pattern a given component uses is still unresolved (Play 8). 223 224 --- 225 226 ## Play 5 — PR review 227 228 *Covers responsibility 4* 229 230 The useful move here is knowing what the tooling already catches, so your attention goes where it's actually needed. 231 232 ### Already mechanical — don't spend review time on it 233 234 | Check | Enforced by | 235 |---|---| 236 | Missing `alt` on `` | ast-grep `img-missing-alt` | 237 | `IconButton` without `aria-label` | ast-grep `icon-button-missing-aria-label` | 238 | `onClick` on non-interactive element without `role` | ast-grep `clickable-non-interactive-element` | 239 | Payment credentials logged | semgrep `payment-credential-logged` | 240 | Unsanitised `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` | semgrep `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` | 241 | Type errors, lint, conventional commits | `tsc --noEmit`, lint, commit-msg hook | 242 | Registry freshness | pre-commit hook | 243 244 ### Not enforced — this is your list 245 246 | Gap | Why it matters | 247 |---|---| 248 | **Hardcoded hex / px values** in Chakra props and `.scss` | `css.md` states plainly it isn't mechanically enforced. Highest-frequency design-system violation | 249 | **Component complexity / size** | No `complexity` or `max-lines-per-function` in `.eslintrc.js` — confirmed | 250 | **Chakra `` without alt** | The ast-grep rule matches lowercase `` only. Every Contentful component here uses `` — so the guard doesn't cover the component family under discussion | 251 | **Duplication / reuse** | No tool detects "this is a second Button". This is the core of responsibility #3 and it is entirely human | 252 | **Salesforce alignment** | Whether base capability was leveraged — judgement only | 253 254 Two of these are cheap to close, and the repo's own rules files already recommend the fix: an ast-grep rule for hardcoded design values, and the two ESLint core rules. **Both touch Tier 1 files** — raise as a decision, don't land quietly. See §Guardrails. 255 256 ### Review questions, in order 257 258 1. Was an existing component / hook / utility reused, or is this a second implementation? 259 2. Are all design values tokens? 260 3. Does it respect existing abstractions, or work around them? 261 4. Was base Salesforce capability leveraged where it exists? 262 5. Accessibility: keyboard, focus order, states — beyond what ast-grep catches 263 6. Storybook story present? Test where logic-heavy? 264 265 --- 266 267 ## Play 6 — Accessibility 268 269 *Covers responsibilities 6, 12* 270 271 M1 and M2 both landed on accessibility living **inside** component stories, as AC, not as a follow-up task. 272 273 ### The per-component AC set (#12) 274 275 Standing list to apply to every component story: 276 277 - Keyboard operability and reachability 278 - Focus order and visible focus states 279 - Interaction states (hover, active, disabled, focused) 280 - Screen-reader behaviour for images and icon-only controls 281 - Behaviour when optional content is absent 282 283 **Baseline is WCAG 2.2 AA**, falling back to 2.1 only where 2.2 is technically infeasible *and* the reason is documented. Worth correcting on SFCC-648, which currently commits to 2.1 AA — and setting 2.2 as the story-template default so it doesn't propagate. 284 285 ### The one open item 286 287 M2 landed on: *if alt text exists render it; if not, don't render the attribute.* There's a real technical problem with that — omitting the attribute makes assistive tech treat the image as meaningful-but-undescribed, and it commonly reads out the filename; `alt=""` removes it from the accessibility tree entirely. The existing draft AC on the render story already says the latter. 288 289 **Your action:** get it confirmed with Tim before it propagates into every image-bearing component. Frame it as the content-model question it really is — *how do we distinguish "intentionally decorative" from "someone forgot"?* — which is a Contentful field decision (required alt, or an explicit decorative toggle), not a renderer decision. The BA guide flags it as pending rather than settled. 290 291 --- 292 293 ## Play 7 — Page-level validation 294 295 *Covers responsibilities 13, 15* 296 297 M2 kept page validation with FED even though pages stop being development units: spacing, layout, design fidelity, responsive behaviour, assembled UX. 298 299 ### Where each part lands today 300 301 | Ask | Home | 302 |---|---| 303 | Assembled UX / integration | ✅ Playwright E2E — `@area` tags `homepage, checkout, search, account, pdp, plp, integrations` | 304 | Performance | ✅ `lighthouserc.js` | 305 | Responsive behaviour | ⚠️ Partial — Playwright runs desktop + mobile Chrome, but asserts behaviour, not appearance | 306 | **Spacing / design fidelity / design parity** | ❌ **No automated home.** `testing.md` explicitly excludes visual snapshots from the Vitest budget | 307 308 **Name this rather than absorbing it.** Design-parity validation is currently manual visual QA. Either it's accepted as manual and the time is resourced, or it's a visual-regression tooling decision (Chromatic / Loki / Percy) — a new dependency and budget, which needs approval before anything is installed. An unresourced ask that quietly becomes yours is the failure mode here. 309 310 Operational note: only `e2e_homepage` is currently mapped in the change-scoping config. Each new area's first spec needs its own allow-list group, or it silently falls back to the full suite. 311 312 ### Incremental assembly (#15) 313 314 Tim's build → drop-in → verify loop is well supported and costs nothing to adopt: 315 316 | Step | Support | 317 |---|---| 318 | Build in isolation | Storybook — mandatory story; `Contentful/` category explicitly allows mock CMS data | 319 | Make available to authors | `npm run generate:contentful` regenerates definitions; pre-commit keeps it in sync | 320 | Author drops it on a page | Studio Experiences — appears once annotated | 321 | Verify | `pages/experience/` and `pages/contentfulPreview/` routes exist | 322 323 **Caveat worth stating:** this loop only works for Studio Experiences components. Entry-driven ones are wired in code and aren't drag-and-droppable. Another reason the pattern question in Play 8 matters. 324 325 --- 326 327 ## Play 8 — Pushing back before sizing 328 329 *Covers responsibility 14* 330 331 These were explicitly left unresolved. Your job is to keep them from being sized on assumption. 332 333 | Open item | Position to hold | 334 |---|---| 335 | **Alt text** | Confirm with Tim before it lands in AC — Play 6 | 336 | **External links** | Already answered in draft AC (internal → same tab; external → new tab + `rel="noopener noreferrer"`). Adopt it, bake it into the Link component when built. Doesn't need another meeting | 337 | **Recommendations** | Not actually unknown — `SFCC-7` already holds eight decomposed, requirement-traced tickets (112, 118, 119, 313, 314, 642, 647, plus 301 under Cart). **SFCC-647 is already `Ready for Development`** and is the one that answers the data-source question. All are Priority `Low`, which is why they surfaced as unknowns. Raise 647; don't create tickets | 338 | **Shop the Look naming** | Four names in circulation for possibly two things: "Shop the Look" (M2 + SFCC-90), "Shop the Edit" (SFCC-313), "Product Cards with Lookbook" (04.7, marked Done), and `shoppableImage` (which already exists in code and delivers exactly the manual curation Bianca described). Resolve to one name per capability before estimating | 339 | **Preview & publishing** | Documented: the preview token is set on dev/test/sit/uat only, never staging or prod; both preview paths 404 without it and are `noindex`. **Authors preview on `uat`.** Settle it now — "can we preview on prod?" is a likely later ask, and it needs a Tier 1 change against a documented security rationale | 340 | **Contentful pattern per component** | Still unresolved after two sessions, and it decides story order, whether the incremental-assembly loop is available, and whether a component is buildable as specified. **Highest-value item to close** | 341 | **`regions` content-model field** | Unconfirmed, and it affects every Contentful component's variant model across 8 storefronts. Prerequisite to "design variants upfront" | 342 | **Composed-page ownership** | Tim's *"not product/category → Contentful"* rule is a good default but doesn't settle PDP/PLP editorial blocks, category landing pages, or promotional tiles in navigation. Category landing pages are the sharp edge, and PLP work is already in flight | 343 344 **A process note worth acting on.** The Size Selector / Add To Bag split was argued and settled in a Jira comment thread two weeks before M1 re-derived it. Decisions made in refinement need somewhere findable to live, or they get re-litigated. Cheapest fix: when a decision lands, it goes on the story *and* into the relevant Confluence page — not just the thread. 345 346 --- 347 348 ## Play 9 — Design-system escalation 349 350 *Covers responsibility 7* 351 352 Standing agenda for the design review with Kiera. Two concrete items rather than a general "validate button states": 353 354 1. **Button** — 04.7 lists *"Style: Primary, Secondary · Size: Large, Small · Colour: Normal, Inverse"* and marks it Done. The implemented component exposes `variant: 'primary'|'secondary'` and `size: 'lg'|'sm'` — **no Colour axis.** Worth noting the *states* are fine (hover, active, disabled, focus-visible are all defined for both variants), so "disabled variants" isn't the gap; the Colour axis is. It already has 5 consumers, so adding it later touches all five. 355 2. **Icon Button** — same Inventory spec, also marked Done, **no implementation at all.** 356 357 More broadly: 04.7's status column marks components Done on *design* confirmation, which doesn't imply the implemented API matches. Worth agreeing what "Done" means in that column, since story writers are reading it as readiness. 358 359 --- 360 361 ## Guardrails 362 363 Things to respect while moving fast on all of the above. 364 365 **Tier 1 files.** You hold tier-1-approver / admin, so the verified-session exception applies — you can proceed after naming the file and the reason. Relevant to Play 5's two proposed rules (`.coderabbit/`, `.eslintrc.js`) and to `.github/workflows/`. 366 367 **Four files are absolute** — the exception does *not* apply regardless of approver status: `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js`. 368 369 **Branches.** Never work on `develop` or `main`. `release/*` is supervised — plan-first, confirm every edit, and code fixes go through a `fix/release-*` sub-branch. 370 371 **Squad boundaries.** `header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/` are shared shell — coordinate with the other squad before touching. `order-summary/` is Tier 2 and Squad B-notified. 372 373 **Commits and PRs** only on explicit request — not as a "natural next step" after finishing work. 374 375 **Scope.** Fixing a bug in a component doesn't license touching the hook it calls. Propose upward refactors; don't do them silently. 376 377 --- 378 379 ## Standing artifacts you own 380 381 | Artifact | Cadence | 382 |---|---| 383 | Refinement checklist (Play 2's challenge list) | Keep current as patterns emerge | 384 | Renderer contract template (Play 4) | Once; sign off per Contentful component | 385 | Per-component accessibility AC set (Play 6) | Once; applied per story | 386 | PR review question list (Play 5) | Review quarterly against what tooling now catches | 387 | Open-items register (Play 8) | Update as items close | 388 | Design-system gap list (Play 9) | Standing design-review agenda | 389 390 --- 391 392 ## First two weeks 393 394 Sequenced by leverage — the first three unblock everything else. 395 396 **Week 1** 397 1. Close the alt-text question with Tim before it propagates into AC 398 2. Get the Contentful pattern decision made (entry-driven vs Studio Experiences per component) — it blocks story order and buildability 399 3. Add the registry line to the BA prompt template — makes Play 1 self-service instead of making you a gate 400 4. Adopt the external-link standard from existing draft AC and close the item 401 402 **Week 2** 403 5. Publish the renderer-contract template and use it on the next Contentful pair 404 6. Communicate the estimation re-baseline once, clearly, in planning 405 7. Take the two Button / Icon Button items to design review 406 8. Raise SFCC-647 so the recommendations question resolves itself 407 9. Put the two enforcement rules up as a decision 408 409 --- 410 411 *Working document. The plays are grounded in what the two sessions actually asked for; the mechanics come from how this repo works today, so both will need updating as the tooling and the backlog move.* 412

Everything below hangs off this. | When | Plays | Time | |---|---|---| | **Story drafting** (BA-initiated, async) | 1 — reuse & dependency check | Async, minutes per story | | **Refinement** (per story) | 1, 3, 9, 14 — dependencies, variants, push-back | In the session | | **Pre-sprint-planning** (weekly) | 2 — estimation validation | ~30 min | | **PR review** (continuous) | 5 — the human-only checks | Per PR | | **Design review** (weekly, with Kiera) | 6 — design-system gaps | Standing slot | Two standing items that don't fit a cadence: the **renderer contract** (Play 4, once per Contentful component) and **page-level validation** (Play 7, once per page assembly). --- ## Play 1 — The reuse & dependency check *Covers responsibilities 1, 2, 3, 8* ### The ladder (agreed in M1) ``` Salesforce / PWA Kit capability ↓ (nothing fits) Existing shared component in overrides/ ↓ (nothing fits) Existing pattern ↓ (nothing fits) New implementation ← justify this out loud ``` ### Where to actually look | Question | Source | |---|---| | Does a Base, Override or Custom component already exist? | `.claude/registry/components.md` — columns: **Origin · Path · Props · Tier · Squad · Consumers**. Regenerated automatically by the pre-commit hook on any `overrides/app/**` change | | Same for hooks / utils / pages / routes | `.claude/registry/{hooks,utils,pages,routes}.md` | | What's in the base package? | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` and `/app/hooks/` | | Is it already claimed by a squad? | Registry `Squad` column · `.claude/rules/squadA.md` | | What tier am I about to touch? | Registry `Tier` column, or `/audit-tier` | The `Origin` column is doing most of the work: **`Base` means it exists but isn't scaffolded into `overrides/` yet** — which is a cost, not a free win (see below). ### Worked examples, already verified | Ask | What already exists | |---|---| | Size selector | Base `swatch-group/` — index, swatch, plus an existing test | | Add to bag | Base `product-view/index.jsx` — already does `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the button and label, the add-to-cart modal, bundle handling, and an `updateCart` variant | | Max purchase quantity | Base `quantity-picker/` | | Variant resolution | `use-controlled-variations`, `use-derived-product`, `use-add-to-cart-modal` | Worth knowing before SFCC-650 is sized: its description says *"Cart API integration is in scope"*, but the base already performs the cart call. That story should read as **extend `product-view`**, not build cart integration. ### The hidden cost to name every time If `Origin = Base`, the component isn't in `overrides/` yet, and AGENTS.md's **Copy-first rule** applies before any functional work: 1. Copy base file → mirrored path in `overrides/` 2. Convert to TypeScript, fix imports 3. `npx tsc --noEmit` 4. Add a temporary `console.log` marker 5. **Stop — a human confirms the override renders instead of the base** 6. Then build; remove markers It's serialised and human-gated. **The first story against a given base component pays it; later ones don't.** This is the single most common reason a story looks small and isn't — exactly Jasmijn's concern. Either split it into an enabler story or size the first story accordingly. ### Making this scale (the fix for #1) Add one line to the BA prompt template in Confluence 274137093: > *"Check `.claude/registry/components.md` — does a Base, Override or Custom component already cover this? Report Origin, Tier, Squad and Consumer count."* That makes four of the six refinement questions self-service. You keep the two that need judgement: - **Is extending the base the right call, or is a Zimmermann-specific build justified?** - **Is the design-system prerequisite real, or can we proceed?** ### Preventing duplicate atoms (#3, #8) The atoms question — *"when does an atom deserve its own story?"* — is largely already answered by existing convention rather than needing a new model: - A story is required for anything **exported from its folder** under `overrides/app/components/` or `/pages/`. - **Not** required for internal sub-components that only render inside one parent — cover their variants via the parent's stories. - The Storybook categorisation (`Foundation / Elements / Layout / Commerce / Forms / Pages / Contentful`) gives you the vocabulary: `Elements/` *is* the atoms layer. Applied to 04.7's `↳ Sub-component` rows: Pause/Play, Footer Item, Footer Textfield, Icons don't each need a story unless independently reusable. Without that rule the Footer alone generates four. --- ## Play 2 — Estimation validation *Covers responsibilities 5, 16* Run this before sprint planning, not in it. ### The re-baseline to communicate once M2 concluded pages become assemblies. The honest consequence: - **Homepage / page estimates should go down.** Composition genuinely is cheaper. - **Component estimates should go up by more than the pages save.** Because a component story now carries: all variants upfront + accessibility AC + a mandatory Storybook story + a test where logic-heavy + Copy-first scaffolding on first touch. If only the first half of that lands, the programme will look like it got faster and won't have. Say this out loud in planning — once, clearly. ### Split the two kinds of effort (#16) | Component build | Page composition | |---|---| | Real frontend development | Assembly and configuration | | Variants, states, accessibility | Integration testing | | Storybook + tests | Visual validation | | Sized as build work | Sized as validation work | Don't let them be estimated with the same scale. ### Challenge list For each story before it's sized: - [ ] `Origin = Base`? → Copy-first cost is in, or split out - [ ] All variants captured, or only the ones on the first page? - [ ] Accessibility written as AC, or assumed? - [ ] Storybook story accounted for? - [ ] Designs confirmed, or still in progress? (04.7 status column) - [ ] Does it depend on anything in Play 8's open list? - [ ] Composition variant hiding as a configuration variant? (Play 3) --- ## Play 3 — Component completeness & variant review *Covers responsibilities 9, 11* M2's rule: a component isn't complete until it covers all supported variants, and the page just configures it. One Editorial Card, not a Homepage one and a PLP one. ### The distinction to hold | Kind | Examples | How it's built | |---|---|---| | **Configuration variant** | text alignment, CTA on/off, title on/off, body copy present/absent | Props on one component ✅ Tim's rule applies directly | | **Composition variant** | 1 vs 2 column, 3-up vs 4-up grids | A **container/slot component** — structurally a second component | This matters because a composition variant priced as a prop will be under-estimated. On the Studio Experiences path especially, a repeating structure can't be a prop — the composition primitive is `children`. So "one Editorial Card with all variants" often resolves to *two* components: the card, plus a container holding one or two. Better outcome — the container is reusable anywhere — but it changes the count. Catch it at refinement. ### Why "upfront" is a hard requirement here, not a preference The Contentful sync is **additive-only — it cannot delete a field from a published content type**. Getting the variant model wrong isn't rework, it's semi-permanent. This is the strongest argument you have for holding the line on variant completeness, and it supports Tim's position rather than fighting it. ### Optional-field handling (#11) M2: don't assume CMS fields are populated. Every Contentful-backed component needs AC for the absent case — no empty space, no placeholder, no layout break. Make it a standing question in refinement rather than a per-story discovery. --- ## Play 4 — The renderer contract *Covers responsibility 10* M2 asked for "a standard renderer contract between Contentful models and React components." This is the artifact that makes the Contentful story and the PWA Kit story independently workable — without it they drift, and additive-only sync makes drift expensive. **The requirement it satisfies:** `02-contentful.md` §2 — *"TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time."* **The artifact:** one table, identical in both stories of every Contentful pair. | Field ID | Display name | Type / control | Required | Localised | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `image` | Image | Media | Yes | No | | | `imageAlt` | Image Alt Text | shortText | No | Yes | behaviour when empty — see Play 6 | | `bodyCopy` | Body Copy | longText | No | Yes | | | `ctaLabel` | CTA Label | shortText | No | Yes | CTA renders only if label **and** URL set | | `ctaUrl` | CTA URL | shortText | No | No | internal → same tab; external → new tab + `rel="noopener noreferrer"` | **Field IDs, not display names.** "Body copy" in prose is where drift starts. **You own the template; the BA fills it; you sign off the field IDs before the Contentful story is built.** That signature is the cheapest possible insurance against an undeletable wrong field. **Note for the ordering question:** for Studio Experiences components the contract is generated from the React props rather than authored first — so the review point moves to the component's prop type. Which pattern a given component uses is still unresolved (Play 8). --- ## Play 5 — PR review *Covers responsibility 4* The useful move here is knowing what the tooling already catches, so your attention goes where it's actually needed. ### Already mechanical — don't spend review time on it | Check | Enforced by | |---|---| | Missing `alt` on `` | ast-grep `img-missing-alt` | | `IconButton` without `aria-label` | ast-grep `icon-button-missing-aria-label` | | `onClick` on non-interactive element without `role` | ast-grep `clickable-non-interactive-element` | | Payment credentials logged | semgrep `payment-credential-logged` | | Unsanitised `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` | semgrep `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` | | Type errors, lint, conventional commits | `tsc --noEmit`, lint, commit-msg hook | | Registry freshness | pre-commit hook | ### Not enforced — this is your list | Gap | Why it matters | |---|---| | **Hardcoded hex / px values** in Chakra props and `.scss` | `css.md` states plainly it isn't mechanically enforced. Highest-frequency design-system violation | | **Component complexity / size** | No `complexity` or `max-lines-per-function` in `.eslintrc.js` — confirmed | | **Chakra `` without alt** | The ast-grep rule matches lowercase `` only. Every Contentful component here uses `` — so the guard doesn't cover the component family under discussion | | **Duplication / reuse** | No tool detects "this is a second Button". This is the core of responsibility #3 and it is entirely human | | **Salesforce alignment** | Whether base capability was leveraged — judgement only | Two of these are cheap to close, and the repo's own rules files already recommend the fix: an ast-grep rule for hardcoded design values, and the two ESLint core rules. **Both touch Tier 1 files** — raise as a decision, don't land quietly. See §Guardrails. ### Review questions, in order 1. Was an existing component / hook / utility reused, or is this a second implementation? 2. Are all design values tokens? 3. Does it respect existing abstractions, or work around them? 4. Was base Salesforce capability leveraged where it exists? 5. Accessibility: keyboard, focus order, states — beyond what ast-grep catches 6. Storybook story present? Test where logic-heavy? --- ## Play 6 — Accessibility *Covers responsibilities 6, 12* M1 and M2 both landed on accessibility living **inside** component stories, as AC, not as a follow-up task. ### The per-component AC set (#12) Standing list to apply to every component story: - Keyboard operability and reachability - Focus order and visible focus states - Interaction states (hover, active, disabled, focused) - Screen-reader behaviour for images and icon-only controls - Behaviour when optional content is absent **Baseline is WCAG 2.2 AA**, falling back to 2.1 only where 2.2 is technically infeasible *and* the reason is documented. Worth correcting on SFCC-648, which currently commits to 2.1 AA — and setting 2.2 as the story-template default so it doesn't propagate. ### The one open item M2 landed on: *if alt text exists render it; if not, don't render the attribute.* There's a real technical problem with that — omitting the attribute makes assistive tech treat the image as meaningful-but-undescribed, and it commonly reads out the filename; `alt=""` removes it from the accessibility tree entirely. The existing draft AC on the render story already says the latter. **Your action:** get it confirmed with Tim before it propagates into every image-bearing component. Frame it as the content-model question it really is — *how do we distinguish "intentionally decorative" from "someone forgot"?* — which is a Contentful field decision (required alt, or an explicit decorative toggle), not a renderer decision. The BA guide flags it as pending rather than settled. --- ## Play 7 — Page-level validation *Covers responsibilities 13, 15* M2 kept page validation with FED even though pages stop being development units: spacing, layout, design fidelity, responsive behaviour, assembled UX. ### Where each part lands today | Ask | Home | |---|---| | Assembled UX / integration | ✅ Playwright E2E — `@area` tags `homepage, checkout, search, account, pdp, plp, integrations` | | Performance | ✅ `lighthouserc.js` | | Responsive behaviour | ⚠️ Partial — Playwright runs desktop + mobile Chrome, but asserts behaviour, not appearance | | **Spacing / design fidelity / design parity** | ❌ **No automated home.** `testing.md` explicitly excludes visual snapshots from the Vitest budget | **Name this rather than absorbing it.** Design-parity validation is currently manual visual QA. Either it's accepted as manual and the time is resourced, or it's a visual-regression tooling decision (Chromatic / Loki / Percy) — a new dependency and budget, which needs approval before anything is installed. An unresourced ask that quietly becomes yours is the failure mode here. Operational note: only `e2e_homepage` is currently mapped in the change-scoping config. Each new area's first spec needs its own allow-list group, or it silently falls back to the full suite. ### Incremental assembly (#15) Tim's build → drop-in → verify loop is well supported and costs nothing to adopt: | Step | Support | |---|---| | Build in isolation | Storybook — mandatory story; `Contentful/` category explicitly allows mock CMS data | | Make available to authors | `npm run generate:contentful` regenerates definitions; pre-commit keeps it in sync | | Author drops it on a page | Studio Experiences — appears once annotated | | Verify | `pages/experience/` and `pages/contentfulPreview/` routes exist | **Caveat worth stating:** this loop only works for Studio Experiences components. Entry-driven ones are wired in code and aren't drag-and-droppable. Another reason the pattern question in Play 8 matters. --- ## Play 8 — Pushing back before sizing *Covers responsibility 14* These were explicitly left unresolved. Your job is to keep them from being sized on assumption. | Open item | Position to hold | |---|---| | **Alt text** | Confirm with Tim before it lands in AC — Play 6 | | **External links** | Already answered in draft AC (internal → same tab; external → new tab + `rel="noopener noreferrer"`). Adopt it, bake it into the Link component when built. Doesn't need another meeting | | **Recommendations** | Not actually unknown — `SFCC-7` already holds eight decomposed, requirement-traced tickets (112, 118, 119, 313, 314, 642, 647, plus 301 under Cart). **SFCC-647 is already `Ready for Development`** and is the one that answers the data-source question. All are Priority `Low`, which is why they surfaced as unknowns. Raise 647; don't create tickets | | **Shop the Look naming** | Four names in circulation for possibly two things: "Shop the Look" (M2 + SFCC-90), "Shop the Edit" (SFCC-313), "Product Cards with Lookbook" (04.7, marked Done), and `shoppableImage` (which already exists in code and delivers exactly the manual curation Bianca described). Resolve to one name per capability before estimating | | **Preview & publishing** | Documented: the preview token is set on dev/test/sit/uat only, never staging or prod; both preview paths 404 without it and are `noindex`. **Authors preview on `uat`.** Settle it now — "can we preview on prod?" is a likely later ask, and it needs a Tier 1 change against a documented security rationale | | **Contentful pattern per component** | Still unresolved after two sessions, and it decides story order, whether the incremental-assembly loop is available, and whether a component is buildable as specified. **Highest-value item to close** | | **`regions` content-model field** | Unconfirmed, and it affects every Contentful component's variant model across 8 storefronts. Prerequisite to "design variants upfront" | | **Composed-page ownership** | Tim's *"not product/category → Contentful"* rule is a good default but doesn't settle PDP/PLP editorial blocks, category landing pages, or promotional tiles in navigation. Category landing pages are the sharp edge, and PLP work is already in flight | **A process note worth acting on.** The Size Selector / Add To Bag split was argued and settled in a Jira comment thread two weeks before M1 re-derived it. Decisions made in refinement need somewhere findable to live, or they get re-litigated. Cheapest fix: when a decision lands, it goes on the story *and* into the relevant Confluence page — not just the thread. --- ## Play 9 — Design-system escalation *Covers responsibility 7* Standing agenda for the design review with Kiera. Two concrete items rather than a general "validate button states": 1. **Button** — 04.7 lists *"Style: Primary, Secondary · Size: Large, Small · Colour: Normal, Inverse"* and marks it Done. The implemented component exposes `variant: 'primary'|'secondary'` and `size: 'lg'|'sm'` — **no Colour axis.** Worth noting the *states* are fine (hover, active, disabled, focus-visible are all defined for both variants), so "disabled variants" isn't the gap; the Colour axis is. It already has 5 consumers, so adding it later touches all five. 2. **Icon Button** — same Inventory spec, also marked Done, **no implementation at all.** More broadly: 04.7's status column marks components Done on *design* confirmation, which doesn't imply the implemented API matches. Worth agreeing what "Done" means in that column, since story writers are reading it as readiness. --- ## Guardrails Things to respect while moving fast on all of the above. **Tier 1 files.** You hold tier-1-approver / admin, so the verified-session exception applies — you can proceed after naming the file and the reason. Close the alt-text question with Tim before it propagates into AC 2. Get the Contentful pattern decision made (entry-driven vs Studio Experiences per component) — it blocks story order and buildability 3. Add the registry line to the BA prompt template — makes Play 1 self-service instead of making you a gate 4. Adopt the external-link standard from existing draft AC and close the item **Week 2** 5. input.content: # FED Manual — Manual UI Build & Delivery **Audience:** Front-end developers building UI on the Zimmermann PWA Kit storefront **Scope:** The manual build path — no Figma-to-React generation. You are writing the components. **Companion:** [fedLead-playbook.md](./fedLead-playbook.md) (lead-facing: governance, refinement, estimation) **Owner:** Marcel Navarro · **Started:** August 2026 > **Assumes** the design foundations branch (`feature/design-tokens-implementation-to-dev`) has > landed on `develop`. Until it does, the token guidance in §5 describes the target, not the > current state of `develop`. --- ## How to use this Read §1–§3 once. After that this is a reference — jump to the section matching what you're doing. The repo's own rules files (`.claude/rules/`) are the source of truth for conventions; this manual is the *sequence* you apply them in, plus the things that aren't written down anywhere. If this manual and a `.claude/rules/` file disagree, the rules file wins and this manual has a bug — tell Marcel. --- ## 1. The build model ### What "manual build" means here We are not generating components from Figma. Every component is hand-written TypeScript against the PWA Kit base, styled with the Zimmermann design tokens, validated against Figma by eye. That makes three things your responsibility that a generator would otherwise have owned: 1. **Finding what already exists** before you build (§3) 2. **Applying tokens correctly** rather than eyeballing hex values off a Figma layer (§5) 3. **Catching design/implementation drift** and reporting it rather than absorbing it (§9) ### Static-first Most integrations aren't live yet — Contentful is on a demo space, SFCC is a sandbox, and Global-e, Omneo, Emarsys, Adyen and the rest haven't started. We are **not** waiting. Build the UI now, fully and properly, with data arriving as props. When the integration comes online, the wiring happens in the page/container above your component and your component doesn't change. **The good news: this is already the repo's rule, not a special mode.** > Anything under `overrides/app/components/` receives data as props — it does not call > data-fetching hooks itself. Data-fetching belongs in `overrides/app/pages/` or another > container component. > — `.claude/rules/components.md` So "static-first" isn't a temporary compromise you'll unwind later. It's the container/presentational split the project already mandates. Follow the rule and you get static-first for free. **What that means concretely:** | Do | Don't | |---|---| | `` | `const {data} = useProduct(id)` inside a leaf component | | Type the prop against the real shape (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic` / Contentful field IDs) | Invent a convenient shape you'll have to migrate | | Drive Storybook from a local mock object | Add MSW handlers to a production path | | Handle the empty/absent case now | Assume every optional field is populated | The last row matters more than it looks. CMS fields are optional far more often than designs imply, and the Contentful sync is **additive-only — it cannot delete a field from a published content type**. A component that breaks when `ctaLabel` is absent is a bug you ship, not a follow-up. ### What we're building on Three sources feed the manual build. Know which one you're drawing from: | Source | What it gives you | Status | |---|---|---| | **PWA Kit base** (`@salesforce/retail-react-app@10.0.0`) | Working components, hooks, commerce logic | Live — check here first, always | | **Design foundations** (`overrides/app/theme/`) | Colour, type, spacing, motion, the brand typeface | Landing now — see §5 | | **Existing F2R outputs** (onshore design team + Jersey) | Primitive/foundation-level components | Incorporate where it fits; don't restart from scratch | Jersey's work is concentrated at the primitive/foundation layer. Treat it the same as any other existing implementation: check it, use it if it fits, extend if it nearly fits, and say so out loud if it doesn't. --- ## 2. Before you write any code Five minutes that save hours. ```bash git branch --show-current ``` **If that returns `develop` or `main`, stop.** Branch first. Everything below assumes you're on `feature/*` or `fix/*`. Then run the session ritual — it reads the tracking docs and does the health checks: ```bash /session-start ``` ### Story intake Before you touch code, you should be able to answer: - [ ] Which `.docs/` requirement am I implementing? (State it — e.g. "per `prd/pdp.md` §3.2") - [ ] Does the story depend on anything in `.docs/memory/projectState.md` → *Unresolved Dependencies*? - [ ] Is anything here from a **later sprint**? Check `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` - [ ] Which squad's territory does this land in? (`.claude/rules/squadA.md` / `squadB.md`) - [ ] What tier are the files I'll touch? That last one: ```bash /audit-tier overrides/app/components/ ``` If a requirement is missing, ambiguous, or contradicts a doc — **stop and ask, one question at a time.** Do not fill the gap with an assumption. This is a hard project rule, not a style preference. --- ## 3. The reuse ladder — do this before building anything The single most common failure mode on this project is building something that already exists. Work down the ladder and stop at the first thing that fits: ``` 1. Salesforce / PWA Kit base capability ↓ nothing fits 2. Existing shared component in overrides/ ↓ nothing fits 3. Existing pattern in the codebase ↓ nothing fits 4. New implementation ← you must justify this out loud ``` ### Where to look | Question | Source | |---|---| | Does a Base, Override or Custom component exist? | `.claude/registry/components.md` | | Same for hooks / utils / pages / routes | `.claude/registry/{hooks,utils,pages,routes}.md` | | What's actually in the base package? | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` | | Is it claimed by a squad? | Registry `Squad` column | | What tier is it? | Registry `Tier` column, or `/audit-tier` | The registry is regenerated automatically by the pre-commit hook, so it's current. ### Worked examples — these are already verified | If the story asks for… | It already exists as… | |---|---| | Size selector | Base `swatch-group/` (index + swatch + a test) | | Add to bag | Base `product-view/index.jsx` — already calls `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, renders the button and label, handles the modal and bundles, and has an `updateCart` variant | | Max purchase quantity | Base `quantity-picker/` | | Variant resolution | `use-controlled-variations`, `use-derived-product`, `use-add-to-cart-modal` | If your story says "integrate the cart API" and the base already makes the cart call, the story is **extend `product-view`** — say so before you start. ### Reading the `Origin` column This is the column that decides how much work you actually have: | Origin | Meaning | Cost | |---|---|---| | `Custom` | Zimmermann-authored, already in `overrides/` | Just build | | `Override` | Base file already copied into `overrides/` | Just build | | `Base` | Exists in the package but **not yet in `overrides/`** | Copy-first tax — see §4 | --- ## 4. The Copy-first rule **When it applies:** any time you need to modify a base component that isn't in `overrides/` yet (`Origin = Base`). **Why it exists:** so you can prove the override is actually rendering before you change its behaviour. Otherwise you spend an afternoon editing a file the app never loads. **The sequence — do not compress it:** 1. Copy the base file → the mirrored path in `overrides/` 2. Convert to TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`), fix imports 3. `npx tsc --noEmit` 4. Add a temporary marker: `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')` 5. **Stop.** A human confirms the override renders instead of the base. 6. Only then make functional changes; remove the markers. **Do all the copies at once,** up front — not one per change. If a story touches four base components, copy all four, typecheck, and present them together. **Two things to know:** - **This is serialised and human-gated.** It is the single most common reason a story looks small and isn't. Flag it at refinement so it's either in the estimate or split into an enabler story. - **Only the first story against a given base component pays it.** Later stories against the same component are cheap. **Naming:** override files keep the original kebab-case filename and folder exactly (`product-tile.tsx`). Zimmermann-authored files are camelCase (`productTile.tsx`). You can tell a file's origin from its name — keep it that way. --- ## 5. Applying the design This is where the manual build differs most from a generated one. Read this section properly. ### Scaffold first ```bash /new-component ``` Gives you the folder, the TypeScript component, and a paired Storybook story in the right shape. ### The type scale — the one trap that will bite you **Use `textStyle`. Never a raw `fontSize` token.** ```tsx … // ✅ … // ❌ ``` Four Zimmermann font-size keys collide with Chakra's defaults, and Chakra's are used at **~199 call sites** across the base app: | Key | Chakra | Zimmermann | |---|---|---| | `md` | 16px | 24px | | `xs` | 12px | 16px | | `2xs` | 10px | 14px | | `3xs` | 7.2px | 12px | The Zimmermann scale is deliberately **not** registered as `theme.fontSizes` — precisely so these never have to agree. If you write `fontSize="md"` you get Chakra's 16px, not the design system's 24px, and it will look like the theme is broken. **Do not "fix" this by registering the Zimmermann scale.** There's a test that will fail (`theme/index.test.tsx` → *scale token collisions*), and if you got past it you'd silently restyle every base component on the site. The same applies to `transition` durations and `sizes` — import the constants directly instead: ```tsx import { iconSizes } from 'app/theme/foundation'; ``` ### The 22 text styles `heading1Strong` `heading1` `heading2` `heading3` · `body1Strong` `body1` `body2Strong` `body2` · `mobileBody1Strong` `mobileBody1` `mobileBody2` · `label` `caption` · `linkLg` `linkSm` · `button` `buttonSm` · `productNames` `price` · `navigation` · `footer` · `serif` Each maps to a named Figma style (`ZIM/h1-strong`, `ZIM/Product-name`, …) — the mapping is in the comments in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`. Browse them rendered in Storybook under **Foundation/Typography**. ### Colour Use the **semantic** names, not the primitives, wherever a semantic one exists: ```tsx // ✅ // ⚠️ primitive // ❌ hardcoded ``` Semantic groups: `text.*` · `background.01–07` · `border.*` · `status.*` · `link.*` · `icon.*` · `action.primary.*` · `action.secondary.*`. Primitives (`grey.*`, `ivory.*`, `coral/green/orange/red.500`, `opacity.*`) exist so semantics can be re-pointed without touching your call site — reach for them only when no semantic name fits. Full swatch reference with token paths: Storybook → **Foundation/Colour**. ### Spacing The named Zimmermann scale is registered as `theme.space` alongside Chakra's numerics: ```tsx // 16px / 32px — design-system scale // Chakra numeric — also valid, less expressive ``` Scale: `3xs` 2 · `2xs` 4 · `xs` 8 · `s` 12 · `m` 16 · `l` 20 · `xl` 24 · `2xl` 32 · `3xl` 40 · `4xl` 64 · `5xl` 80 · `6xl` 128 · `7xl` 160 (px). Prefer the named scale when you're expressing a design-system value — it reads as intent rather than arithmetic. Storybook → **Foundation/Spacing**. ### No hardcoded design values — ever ```tsx // ❌ // ✅ ``` **This is not mechanically enforced yet** — no ast-grep rule, no lint rule. It is caught in human PR review, and it is the highest-frequency design-system violation on the project. Police it in your own diff before someone else does. If a Figma value has no token, that's a **finding, not a licence to hardcode**. See §9. ### The `.zimm-*` global classes — hold off for now The design system also ships 36 `.zimm-*` global classes (`.zimm-text-body1`, `.zimm-btn-primary`, `.zimm-form-row`, `.zimm-grid`, …) mirroring the Chakra surface for pasting handover markup. **Known issue:** the `--zimm-*` CSS variables they depend on are injected by `_app-config`, which Storybook and unit tests never render. In those contexts all 44 referenced variables resolve to nothing — borders vanish, type falls back, the grid loses its padding. **Until that's fixed: use Chakra props and `textStyle`.** They work everywhere. Don't put raw `var(--zimm-*)` strings into Chakra style props either, for the same reason — you'll see that pattern in `theme/components/button.ts`, and it's the thing being fixed, not the thing to copy. ### `.scss` — the last resort Chakra props first. Reach for a co-located `.scss` file only when Chakra genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors, keyframes, print styles). Before you do, try Chakra's `sx` prop or a theme variant — both keep the style next to the JSX. If you do write `.scss`: same filename as the component, scoped to that component only, nesting ≤ 3 levels, no ID selectors, no `!important` without an inline reason. ### Icons ```tsx import { SearchIcon } from 'app/components/icons'; // ✅ single source of truth ``` Never import from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons` directly. If the icon you need isn't in the overrides set, **ask** — don't substitute a visually different one. --- ## 6. Building the component ### Folder layout ``` overrides/app/components/productTile/ index.tsx ← the component index.stories.tsx ← required index.test.ts ← only if logic-heavy types.ts ← only if shared with sibling files productTile.scss ← only if Chakra props are insufficient ``` Import as `import { ProductTile } from 'app/components/productTile'`. ### Rules that apply to every file - **TypeScript only inside `overrides/`.** No `.js`/`.jsx`. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before you finish. - **Named export matching the folder** — `productTile/` exports `ProductTile`. - **Props type named after the component** — `ProductTileProps`. Declare it at the top of the file; move it to `types.ts` only when a sibling file consumes it. - **Callback props are `onEventName`** — `onAddToCart`, `onClose`. - **Required props are non-optional.** Optional props use `?`, not `| undefined`. - **No `any`** without an inline comment explaining why a narrower type is impossible. Prefer `unknown` + a type guard. - **`import type`** for type-only imports. - **Australian spelling** in Zimmermann-authored identifiers and copy — `colour`, `centre`, `organisation`. Override files keep upstream Salesforce spelling verbatim. - **No magic numbers or strings.** Named constant or config module. - **No `console.log`** outside error boundaries or dev tooling — including the Copy-first markers, which come out once confirmed. - **JSDoc required** on any component with ≥2 callers and on every exported hook. Don't re-declare types that `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` or `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` already export — import them. ### When to split - Component function past **~150 lines**, or branching past ~10–15 paths → split it. - **≥2 related `useState` that change together** → extract to a hook (`overrides/app/hooks/use.ts`). - **A `useEffect` with a non-trivial dependency array or a cleanup function** → extract to a hook. - **≥4 `useState` calls** → stop and ask whether this should be a hook. Neither the size nor the complexity limit is ESLint-enforced today. They're self-checks, and `/code-quality` flags them. ### Variants — all of them, upfront A component isn't complete until it covers every supported variant; the page then just configures it. One Editorial Card, not a Homepage one and a PLP one. Know the difference, because it changes the component count: | Kind | Examples | How it's built | |---|---|---| | **Configuration variant** | alignment, CTA on/off, title on/off | Props on one component | | **Composition variant** | 1 vs 2 column, 3-up vs 4-up | A **container/slot component** — structurally a second component | A composition variant priced as a prop will be under-estimated. On Studio Experiences the composition primitive is `children` — a repeating structure genuinely can't be a prop. Flag it at refinement, not mid-build. --- ## 7. Accessibility **Baseline is WCAG 2.2 AA.** Fall back to 2.1 AA only where 2.2 is technically infeasible, and document why. If a story says 2.1 AA, that's a story bug — raise it. ### Already mechanical — don't burn review time on these | Check | Enforced by | |---|---| | `` without `alt` | ast-grep `img-missing-alt` | | `IconButton` without `aria-label` | ast-grep `icon-button-missing-aria-label` | | `onClick` on a non-interactive element without `role` | ast-grep `clickable-non-interactive-element` | | Unsanitised `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` | semgrep | Get these right at authoring time — they fail the PR, not your local build. ### Your list — nothing catches these Apply to every component: - **Keyboard operability** — everything interactive reachable and operable by keyboard - **Focus order** — logical, and focus is visibly indicated - **Interaction states** — hover, active, disabled, focused all defined - **Screen-reader behaviour** — for images and icon-only controls - **Absent optional content** — no empty space, no placeholder, no layout break - **Target size** — 24×24 CSS px minimum (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8) Two known gaps to compensate for manually: - **Chakra `` is not covered** by the alt-text rule — it only matches lowercase ``. Most components here use ``. Check it yourself. - **The alt-text content-model question is open.** Use `alt=""` for genuinely decorative images (removes it from the accessibility tree). Omitting the attribute entirely makes assistive tech treat the image as meaningful-but-undescribed and often read the filename. Don't invent a third behaviour — if a design implies one, raise it. If a real component uses `role`/`tabIndex`/`onKeyDown` to make a `div` interactive, ask first whether a `Button` would be simpler. It almost always is. --- ## 8. Storybook Every component exported from its folder needs a story. Not optional. **Not** required for internal sub-components that only render inside one parent — cover their variants through the parent's stories. (Without that rule the Footer alone generates four.) ### Categorisation — pick the first that matches | Category | What goes here | |---|---| | `Foundation/` | Design tokens — Colour, Typography, Spacing, Icons | | `Elements/` | Generic building blocks — Badge, Tag, Link, Button, Input, Checkbox | | `Layout/` | Global chrome and structure — Header, Footer, DrawerMenu, Breadcrumb, Seo | | `Commerce/` | Commerce-specific shared — ProductTile, OrderSummary, DisplayPrice, SwatchGroup | | `Forms/` | Composed form assemblies — AddressForm, NewsletterSignup | | `Pages/` | Full page assemblies | | `Contentful/` | CMS-driven — use mock Contentful data so variants are visible without a live CMS | Tiebreaker for `Elements/` vs `Forms/`: *can it be used outside a form?* → `Elements/`. ```ts export default { title: 'Commerce/ProductTile' }; // ✅ export default { title: 'Elements/DisplayPrice' }; // ❌ commerce-specific → Commerce/ ``` ### Story content - Every story file has a `Default` export. - Add named exports for meaningful states (`Loading`, `OutOfStock`, `WithDiscount`) — not every prop permutation. - Add a `play` function only when there's interactive behaviour worth asserting. Query through `within(canvasElement)`, prefer `getByRole` with an accessible name, and import `userEvent` from `@storybook/test` (not `@testing-library/user-event`) so it logs in the timeline. A11y runs at `test: 'error'` in CI — a violation fails the build. --- ## 9. Figma is a live reference, not a one-time input Figma stays open throughout the build. You're using it for five things, and only the first is "what does this look like": 1. **Build reference** — layout, spacing, states 2. **Validate the build against the design** — after you build, compare 3. **Spot missing tokens** — a Figma value with no token behind it 4. **Spot missing design definitions** — a state, variant or breakpoint that was never designed 5. **Catch discrepancies** between design and implementation ### When Figma and the tokens disagree **Do not silently pick one.** Both outcomes are findings: | Situation | What to do | |---|---| | Figma value has no token | Raise with design. Don't hardcode; don't invent a token | | Token exists but Figma shows something else | Raise it — one of them is stale | | A state/variant isn't designed | Raise before building. Don't invent it | | Figma contradicts a confirmed PRD | **Stop.** Cite the doc, section and requirement ID, and ask | Two live examples of why this matters: - The Figma file currently references **`FONTSPRING DEMO - Futura Round Medium`** — a trial font with a reduced character set — while the build ships the licensed Futura Round. Spacing measured off those layers may not match what renders. - **`Neue Haas Grotesk Text Std`** appears in Figma but exists nowhere in the design tokens. Neither is something a FED should resolve alone. Both are exactly what "surface gaps that need resolving" means. --- ## 10. Testing Three layers. **Pick the cheapest one that proves the behaviour — don't duplicate across layers.** | Layer | Tool | Covers | File | |---|---|---|---| | Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms | `*.test.ts` co-located | | Interaction | Storybook `play` | Clicks, form fills, focus, disclosure | in `*.stories.tsx` | | E2E | Playwright | Full journeys, multi-region, integration boundaries | `e2e/tests/zimm/` | **Write a test where failure would be non-obvious or costly to debug:** ✅ Data mapping (Contentful → props, locale/currency transforms, SFCC payload → view model) · integration boundaries · complex state (cart mutations, consent, multi-step flows) · pure logic that would break invisibly in a refactor ❌ Re-exports and one-line passthroughs · visual snapshots · the framework itself (that React renders, that Chakra applies styles) E2E specs are **gherkin-first**: a `.feature` file goes to Lead QA in plain English, and no Playwright is written until it's signed off. Use `/qa-generate`. ```bash npm test # Vitest npx tsc --noEmit # types npm run lint # ESLint ``` --- ## 11. Before you open the PR ```bash /code-quality # audit the diff /pr-checklist # generate the description + checklist ``` Then a local CodeRabbit review — **required, not optional**: ```bash cr review --light --base develop ``` If the CLI isn't authenticated: `coderabbit auth status`, then `coderabbit auth login --api-key "$CODERABBIT_API_KEY"` (`npm run env -- init` pulls the shared key). Findings are advisory — use judgement on fix-now vs let-the-PR-review-catch-it — but the review has to actually run. ### Self-check - [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean - [ ] `npm test` passes - [ ] `npm run lint` clean **for the files I touched** - [ ] No hardcoded hex or px in Chakra props or `.scss` - [ ] `textStyle` used, not raw `fontSize` - [ ] Storybook story exists and is in the right category - [ ] Test where logic-heavy - [ ] Accessibility list from §7 walked, not assumed - [ ] Empty/absent state handled for every optional prop - [ ] Copy-first `console.log` markers removed - [ ] No new MSW handlers in a production path - [ ] Reused what existed, or can justify why not - [ ] Only one protection tier touched ### After CodeRabbit reviews the PR **Reply in-thread to every finding — fixed or not.** CodeRabbit learns from PR conversation, so silence teaches it nothing and a good explanation teaches it to stop flagging a non-issue. - Fixed → short reply confirming it, referencing the commit - Not fixing because it conflicts with a repo rule → say which rule or doc, so it learns the pattern A fix commit with no reply doesn't count. Never silently dismiss. --- ## 12. Guardrails ### Branches | Branch | Allowed | |---|---| | `feature/*`, `fix/*` | ✅ Your normal working context | | `release/*` | ⚠️ Supervised — plan-first, confirm every edit; code fixes go via a `fix/release-*` sub-branch | | `hotfix/*` | ✅ Urgent production only | | `develop`, `main` | ❌ **Never** | ### Tiers | Tier | What | Rule | |---|---|---| | **1 — Frozen** | `theme/foundation/`, `static/fonts/`, commerce SDK hooks, `config/`, CI, `.claude/rules/` | Named owner approval. Design tokens go through the UI designer | | **2 — Protected** | `header/`, `footer/`, `product-tile/`, `theme/components/`, `theme/globalStyles.ts`, translations | PR review from someone who isn't the author | | **3/4** | Feature-local | Normal review | **Four files are absolute** — no exception, no approver: `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js`. **Never touch more than one tier in a single change** without confirming scope first. ### Squad boundaries Squad A owns home/PDP/PLP/cart/checkout + `header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/`. Squad B owns search/account/store-locator + `search/`, `store-locator/`. Message the other squad's lead before touching their territory. `product-tile/` and `product-item/` are shared Tier 2 — notify Squad A. ### Scope - **Never refactor upward.** Fixing a bug in a component doesn't license changing the hook it calls. - **Never rename or move a shared hook or component.** - **Never add or remove a package** without integration team approval. When approved, use `npm install` — don't hand-edit `package.json`. - **Never delete files** unless asked in the current prompt. Propose it instead. - **Don't remove existing comments or commented-out code** — leave them for a human. - **Never commit, push, or open a PR** unless explicitly asked in that moment. Finishing the work is not an instruction to commit it. ### Performance — every UI change Mobile LCP budget is **≤ 2s at p75**, and it's a top project priority. - Images always lazy-loaded and correctly sized. Never render a full-res image at thumbnail size. - Prefer dynamic `import()` for heavy components not needed on first render. - Request only the fields you need; parallelise — waterfall requests aren't acceptable. - No third-party script before Didomi consent is granted. If consent state is unknown, load nothing. - Check `package.json` before reaching for a library. If a new one is genuinely needed, present the trade-off and wait for approval. --- ## 13. When to stop and ask | Trigger | Action | |---|---| | Requirement missing, ambiguous, or contradicts `.docs/` | Stop. Flag, propose, wait | | Task needs a Tier 1 file | Stop. Named owner approval | | A shared hook needs its signature changed | Stop. Team RFC | | A new package is needed | Stop. Integration team | | Change affects more than one regional site config | Stop. Integration sign-off | | Change spans multiple tiers | Stop. Confirm scope | | Story depends on a later sprint | Stop. Ask before building a placeholder | | On `develop` or `main` | Stop immediately | **Ask one question at a time.** Don't batch them, and don't proceed on the assumption while you wait. ### Ask in the group chat, not in your head Working something out solo that three other people already know is the most expensive habit on a team this size. The expectation is explicit: **FEDs and the wider tech team ask more questions in group channels rather than solving alone.** Those threads are how the group learns — including the questions that turn out to have obvious answers. Claude is part of the workflow where it fits. It isn't a substitute for asking a person when the answer is a project decision rather than a technical one. --- ## 14. Quick reference ### Commands ```bash git branch --show-current # always, first npx tsc --noEmit # types npm test # Vitest npm run lint # ESLint npm run storybook # Storybook on :6006 cr review --light --base develop # pre-commit review ``` `npm start` — **don't run it.** Ask for a restart if you need one. ### Skills | Skill | Use | |---|---| | `/session-start` | Every session — tracking docs + health checks | | `/new-component` | Scaffold a component + story | | `/audit-tier` | Tier, owner and blast radius of a path | | `/scope-check` | Sanity-check a risky prompt before running it | | `/code-quality` | Audit the diff before a PR | | `/pr-checklist` | Generate PR description + checklist | | `/qa-generate` | Gherkin `.feature` → Playwright, after QA sign-off | | `/feature-spec` | Turn a plain-English request into a scoped plan | | `/contentful-register-component` | Register a component with Studio Experiences | ### Paths ``` overrides/app/components/ your components overrides/app/pages/ containers — data fetching lives HERE overrides/app/hooks/ shared hooks overrides/app/theme/ foundation/ = Tier 1 tokens · components/ = Tier 2 overrides overrides/app/types/ commerce.ts · components.ts · hooks.ts .claude/registry/ what already exists — check before building .claude/rules/ the conventions, in full .docs/prd/ requirements — the source of truth .docs/memory/projectState.md unresolved dependencies ``` --- ## The five that matter most If you remember nothing else: 1. **Check the registry before you build.** Most things already exist. 2. **`textStyle`, never `fontSize`.** The scales collide and it looks like a broken theme. 3. **Data as props.** Never fetch inside a component — that's what makes static-first work. 4. **A Figma value with no token is a finding, not a licence to hardcode.** 5. **Ask in the channel.** One question at a time, before the assumption becomes code. --- *Working document. Conventions come from `.claude/rules/` and `AGENTS.md` — if they change, they change there first and this follows. Raise corrections with Marcel.*
