toolUseResult.content: # FED Manual — Manual UI Build & Delivery **Audience:** Front-end developers building UI on the Zimmermann PWA Kit storefront **Scope:** The manual build path — no Figma-to-React generation. You are writing the components. **Companion:** [fedLead-playbook.md](./fedLead-playbook.md) (lead-facing: governance, refinement, estimation) **Owner:** Marcel Navarro · **Started:** August 2026 > **Assumes** the design foundations branch (`feature/design-tokens-implementation-to-dev`) has > landed on `develop`. Until it does, the token guidance in §5 describes the target, not the > current state of `develop`. --- ## How to use this Read §1–§3 once. After that this is a reference — jump to the section matching what you're doing. The repo's own rules files (`.claude/rules/`) are the source of truth for conventions; this manual is the *sequence* you apply them in, plus the things that aren't written down anywhere. If this manual and a `.claude/rules/` file disagree, the rules file wins and this manual has a bug — tell Marcel. --- ## 1. The build model ### What "manual build" means here We are not generating components from Figma. Every component is hand-written TypeScript against the PWA Kit base, styled with the Zimmermann design tokens, validated against Figma by eye. That makes three things your responsibility that a generator would otherwise have owned: 1. **Finding what already exists** before you build (§3) 2. **Applying tokens correctly** rather than eyeballing hex values off a Figma layer (§5) 3. **Catching design/implementation drift** and reporting it rather than absorbing it (§9) ### Static-first Most integrations aren't live yet — Contentful is on a demo space, SFCC is a sandbox, and Global-e, Omneo, Emarsys, Adyen and the rest haven't started. We are **not** waiting. Build the UI now, fully and properly, with data arriving as props. When the integration comes online, the wiring happens in the page/container above your component and your component doesn't change. **The good news: this is already the repo's rule, not a special mode.** > Anything under `overrides/app/components/` receives data as props — it does not call > data-fetching hooks itself. Data-fetching belongs in `overrides/app/pages/` or another > container component. > — `.claude/rules/components.md` So "static-first" isn't a temporary compromise you'll unwind later. It's the container/presentational split the project already mandates. Follow the rule and you get static-first for free. **What that means concretely:** | Do | Don't | |---|---| | `` | `const {data} = useProduct(id)` inside a leaf component | | Type the prop against the real shape (`commerce-sdk-isomorphic` / Contentful field IDs) | Invent a convenient shape you'll have to migrate | | Drive Storybook from a local mock object | Add MSW handlers to a production path | | Handle the empty/absent case now | Assume every optional field is populated | The last row matters more than it looks. CMS fields are optional far more often than designs imply, and the Contentful sync is **additive-only — it cannot delete a field from a published content type**. A component that breaks when `ctaLabel` is absent is a bug you ship, not a follow-up. ### What we're building on Three sources feed the manual build. Know which one you're drawing from: | Source | What it gives you | Status | |---|---|---| | **PWA Kit base** (`@salesforce/retail-react-app@10.0.0`) | Working components, hooks, commerce logic | Live — check here first, always | | **Design foundations** (`overrides/app/theme/`) | Colour, type, spacing, motion, the brand typeface | Landing now — see §5 | | **Existing F2R outputs** (onshore design team + Jersey) | Primitive/foundation-level components | Incorporate where it fits; don't restart from scratch | Jersey's work is concentrated at the primitive/foundation layer. Treat it the same as any other existing implementation: check it, use it if it fits, extend if it nearly fits, and say so out loud if it doesn't. --- ## 2. Before you write any code Five minutes that save hours. ```bash git branch --show-current ``` **If that returns `develop` or `main`, stop.** Branch first. Everything below assumes you're on `feature/*` or `fix/*`. Then run the session ritual — it reads the tracking docs and does the health checks: ```bash /session-start ``` ### Story intake Before you touch code, you should be able to answer: - [ ] Which `.docs/` requirement am I implementing? (State it — e.g. "per `prd/pdp.md` §3.2") - [ ] Does the story depend on anything in `.docs/memory/projectState.md` → *Unresolved Dependencies*? - [ ] Is anything here from a **later sprint**? Check `.docs/memory/sprintScope.md` - [ ] Which squad's territory does this land in? (`.claude/rules/squadA.md` / `squadB.md`) - [ ] What tier are the files I'll touch? That last one: ```bash /audit-tier overrides/app/components/ ``` If a requirement is missing, ambiguous, or contradicts a doc — **stop and ask, one question at a time.** Do not fill the gap with an assumption. This is a hard project rule, not a style preference. --- ## 3. The reuse ladder — do this before building anything The single most common failure mode on this project is building something that already exists. Work down the ladder and stop at the first thing that fits: ``` 1. Salesforce / PWA Kit base capability ↓ nothing fits 2. Existing shared component in overrides/ ↓ nothing fits 3. Existing pattern in the codebase ↓ nothing fits 4. New implementation ← you must justify this out loud ``` ### Where to look | Question | Source | |---|---| | Does a Base, Override or Custom component exist? | `.claude/registry/components.md` | | Same for hooks / utils / pages / routes | `.claude/registry/{hooks,utils,pages,routes}.md` | | What's actually in the base package? | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` | | Is it claimed by a squad? | Registry `Squad` column | | What tier is it? | Registry `Tier` column, or `/audit-tier` | The registry is regenerated automatically by the pre-commit hook, so it's current. ### Worked examples — these are already verified | If the story asks for… | It already exists as… | |---|---| | Size selector | Base `swatch-group/` (index + swatch + a test) | | Add to bag | Base `product-view/index.jsx` — already calls `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, renders the button and label, handles the modal and bundles, and has an `updateCart` variant | | Max purchase quantity | Base `quantity-picker/` | | Variant resolution | `use-controlled-variations`, `use-derived-product`, `use-add-to-cart-modal` | If your story says "integrate the cart API" and the base already makes the cart call, the story is **extend `product-view`** — say so before you start. ### Reading the `Origin` column This is the column that decides how much work you actually have: | Origin | Meaning | Cost | |---|---|---| | `Custom` | Zimmermann-authored, already in `overrides/` | Just build | | `Override` | Base file already copied into `overrides/` | Just build | | `Base` | Exists in the package but **not yet in `overrides/`** | Copy-first tax — see §4 | --- ## 4. The Copy-first rule **When it applies:** any time you need to modify a base component that isn't in `overrides/` yet (`Origin = Base`). **Why it exists:** so you can prove the override is actually rendering before you change its behaviour. Otherwise you spend an afternoon editing a file the app never loads. **The sequence — do not compress it:** 1. Copy the base file → the mirrored path in `overrides/` 2. Convert to TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`), fix imports 3. `npx tsc --noEmit` 4. Add a temporary marker: `console.log('[overrides] product-tile.tsx')` 5. **Stop.** A human confirms the override renders instead of the base. 6. Only then make functional changes; remove the markers. **Do all the copies at once,** up front — not one per change. If a story touches four base components, copy all four, typecheck, and present them together. **Two things to know:** - **This is serialised and human-gated.** It is the single most common reason a story looks small and isn't. Flag it at refinement so it's either in the estimate or split into an enabler story. - **Only the first story against a given base component pays it.** Later stories against the same component are cheap. **Naming:** override files keep the original kebab-case filename and folder exactly (`product-tile.tsx`). Zimmermann-authored files are camelCase (`productTile.tsx`). You can tell a file's origin from its name — keep it that way. --- ## 5. Applying the design This is where the manual build differs most from a generated one. Read this section properly. ### Scaffold first ```bash /new-component ``` Gives you the folder, the TypeScript component, and a paired Storybook story in the right shape. ### The type scale — the one trap that will bite you **Use `textStyle`. Never a raw `fontSize` token.** ```tsx … // ✅ … // ❌ ``` Four Zimmermann font-size keys collide with Chakra's defaults, and Chakra's are used at **~199 call sites** across the base app: | Key | Chakra | Zimmermann | |---|---|---| | `md` | 16px | 24px | | `xs` | 12px | 16px | | `2xs` | 10px | 14px | | `3xs` | 7.2px | 12px | The Zimmermann scale is deliberately **not** registered as `theme.fontSizes` — precisely so these never have to agree. If you write `fontSize="md"` you get Chakra's 16px, not the design system's 24px, and it will look like the theme is broken. **Do not "fix" this by registering the Zimmermann scale.** There's a test that will fail (`theme/index.test.tsx` → *scale token collisions*), and if you got past it you'd silently restyle every base component on the site. The same applies to `transition` durations and `sizes` — import the constants directly instead: ```tsx import { iconSizes } from 'app/theme/foundation'; ``` ### The 22 text styles `heading1Strong` `heading1` `heading2` `heading3` · `body1Strong` `body1` `body2Strong` `body2` · `mobileBody1Strong` `mobileBody1` `mobileBody2` · `label` `caption` · `linkLg` `linkSm` · `button` `buttonSm` · `productNames` `price` · `navigation` · `footer` · `serif` Each maps to a named Figma style (`ZIM/h1-strong`, `ZIM/Product-name`, …) — the mapping is in the comments in `theme/foundation/typography.ts`. Browse them rendered in Storybook under **Foundation/Typography**. ### Colour Use the **semantic** names, not the primitives, wherever a semantic one exists: ```tsx // ✅ // ⚠️ primitive // ❌ hardcoded ``` Semantic groups: `text.*` · `background.01–07` · `border.*` · `status.*` · `link.*` · `icon.*` · `action.primary.*` · `action.secondary.*`. Primitives (`grey.*`, `ivory.*`, `coral/green/orange/red.500`, `opacity.*`) exist so semantics can be re-pointed without touching your call site — reach for them only when no semantic name fits. Full swatch reference with token paths: Storybook → **Foundation/Colour**. ### Spacing The named Zimmermann scale is registered as `theme.space` alongside Chakra's numerics: ```tsx // 16px / 32px — design-system scale // Chakra numeric — also valid, less expressive ``` Scale: `3xs` 2 · `2xs` 4 · `xs` 8 · `s` 12 · `m` 16 · `l` 20 · `xl` 24 · `2xl` 32 · `3xl` 40 · `4xl` 64 · `5xl` 80 · `6xl` 128 · `7xl` 160 (px). Prefer the named scale when you're expressing a design-system value — it reads as intent rather than arithmetic. Storybook → **Foundation/Spacing**. ### No hardcoded design values — ever ```tsx // ❌ // ✅ ``` **This is not mechanically enforced yet** — no ast-grep rule, no lint rule. It is caught in human PR review, and it is the highest-frequency design-system violation on the project. Police it in your own diff before someone else does. If a Figma value has no token, that's a **finding, not a licence to hardcode**. See §9. ### The `.zimm-*` global classes — hold off for now The design system also ships 36 `.zimm-*` global classes (`.zimm-text-body1`, `.zimm-btn-primary`, `.zimm-form-row`, `.zimm-grid`, …) mirroring the Chakra surface for pasting handover markup. **Known issue:** the `--zimm-*` CSS variables they depend on are injected by `_app-config`, which Storybook and unit tests never render. In those contexts all 44 referenced variables resolve to nothing — borders vanish, type falls back, the grid loses its padding. **Until that's fixed: use Chakra props and `textStyle`.** They work everywhere. Don't put raw `var(--zimm-*)` strings into Chakra style props either, for the same reason — you'll see that pattern in `theme/components/button.ts`, and it's the thing being fixed, not the thing to copy. ### `.scss` — the last resort Chakra props first. Reach for a co-located `.scss` file only when Chakra genuinely can't express it (complex pseudo-selectors, keyframes, print styles). Before you do, try Chakra's `sx` prop or a theme variant — both keep the style next to the JSX. If you do write `.scss`: same filename as the component, scoped to that component only, nesting ≤ 3 levels, no ID selectors, no `!important` without an inline reason. ### Icons ```tsx import { SearchIcon } from 'app/components/icons'; // ✅ single source of truth ``` Never import from `@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/icons` directly. If the icon you need isn't in the overrides set, **ask** — don't substitute a visually different one. --- ## 6. Building the component ### Folder layout ``` overrides/app/components/productTile/ index.tsx ← the component index.stories.tsx ← required index.test.ts ← only if logic-heavy types.ts ← only if shared with sibling files productTile.scss ← only if Chakra props are insufficient ``` Import as `import { ProductTile } from 'app/components/productTile'`. ### Rules that apply to every file - **TypeScript only inside `overrides/`.** No `.js`/`.jsx`. Run `npx tsc --noEmit` before you finish. - **Named export matching the folder** — `productTile/` exports `ProductTile`. - **Props type named after the component** — `ProductTileProps`. Declare it at the top of the file; move it to `types.ts` only when a sibling file consumes it. - **Callback props are `onEventName`** — `onAddToCart`, `onClose`. - **Required props are non-optional.** Optional props use `?`, not `| undefined`. - **No `any`** without an inline comment explaining why a narrower type is impossible. Prefer `unknown` + a type guard. - **`import type`** for type-only imports. - **Australian spelling** in Zimmermann-authored identifiers and copy — `colour`, `centre`, `organisation`. Override files keep upstream Salesforce spelling verbatim. - **No magic numbers or strings.** Named constant or config module. - **No `console.log`** outside error boundaries or dev tooling — including the Copy-first markers, which come out once confirmed. - **JSDoc required** on any component with ≥2 callers and on every exported hook. Don't re-declare types that `commerce-sdk-isomorphic` or `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` already export — import them. ### When to split - Component function past **~150 lines**, or branching past ~10–15 paths → split it. - **≥2 related `useState` that change together** → extract to a hook (`overrides/app/hooks/use.ts`). - **A `useEffect` with a non-trivial dependency array or a cleanup function** → extract to a hook. - **≥4 `useState` calls** → stop and ask whether this should be a hook. Neither the size nor the complexity limit is ESLint-enforced today. They're self-checks, and `/code-quality` flags them. ### Variants — all of them, upfront A component isn't complete until it covers every supported variant; the page then just configures it. One Editorial Card, not a Homepage one and a PLP one. Know the difference, because it changes the component count: | Kind | Examples | How it's built | |---|---|---| | **Configuration variant** | alignment, CTA on/off, title on/off | Props on one component | | **Composition variant** | 1 vs 2 column, 3-up vs 4-up | A **container/slot component** — structurally a second component | A composition variant priced as a prop will be under-estimated. On Studio Experiences the composition primitive is `children` — a repeating structure genuinely can't be a prop. Flag it at refinement, not mid-build. --- ## 7. Accessibility **Baseline is WCAG 2.2 AA.** Fall back to 2.1 AA only where 2.2 is technically infeasible, and document why. If a story says 2.1 AA, that's a story bug — raise it. ### Already mechanical — don't burn review time on these | Check | Enforced by | |---|---| | `` without `alt` | ast-grep `img-missing-alt` | | `IconButton` without `aria-label` | ast-grep `icon-button-missing-aria-label` | | `onClick` on a non-interactive element without `role` | ast-grep `clickable-non-interactive-element` | | Unsanitised `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` | semgrep | Get these right at authoring time — they fail the PR, not your local build. ### Your list — nothing catches these Apply to every component: - **Keyboard operability** — everything interactive reachable and operable by keyboard - **Focus order** — logical, and focus is visibly indicated - **Interaction states** — hover, active, disabled, focused all defined - **Screen-reader behaviour** — for images and icon-only controls - **Absent optional content** — no empty space, no placeholder, no layout break - **Target size** — 24×24 CSS px minimum (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8) Two known gaps to compensate for manually: - **Chakra `` is not covered** by the alt-text rule — it only matches lowercase ``. Most components here use ``. Check it yourself. - **The alt-text content-model question is open.** Use `alt=""` for genuinely decorative images (removes it from the accessibility tree). Omitting the attribute entirely makes assistive tech treat the image as meaningful-but-undescribed and often read the filename. Don't invent a third behaviour — if a design implies one, raise it. If a real component uses `role`/`tabIndex`/`onKeyDown` to make a `div` interactive, ask first whether a `Button` would be simpler. It almost always is. --- ## 8. Storybook Every component exported from its folder needs a story. Not optional. **Not** required for internal sub-components that only render inside one parent — cover their variants through the parent's stories. (Without that rule the Footer alone generates four.) ### Categorisation — pick the first that matches | Category | What goes here | |---|---| | `Foundation/` | Design tokens — Colour, Typography, Spacing, Icons | | `Elements/` | Generic building blocks — Badge, Tag, Link, Button, Input, Checkbox | | `Layout/` | Global chrome and structure — Header, Footer, DrawerMenu, Breadcrumb, Seo | | `Commerce/` | Commerce-specific shared — ProductTile, OrderSummary, DisplayPrice, SwatchGroup | | `Forms/` | Composed form assemblies — AddressForm, NewsletterSignup | | `Pages/` | Full page assemblies | | `Contentful/` | CMS-driven — use mock Contentful data so variants are visible without a live CMS | Tiebreaker for `Elements/` vs `Forms/`: *can it be used outside a form?* → `Elements/`. ```ts export default { title: 'Commerce/ProductTile' }; // ✅ export default { title: 'Elements/DisplayPrice' }; // ❌ commerce-specific → Commerce/ ``` ### Story content - Every story file has a `Default` export. - Add named exports for meaningful states (`Loading`, `OutOfStock`, `WithDiscount`) — not every prop permutation. - Add a `play` function only when there's interactive behaviour worth asserting. Query through `within(canvasElement)`, prefer `getByRole` with an accessible name, and import `userEvent` from `@storybook/test` (not `@testing-library/user-event`) so it logs in the timeline. A11y runs at `test: 'error'` in CI — a violation fails the build. --- ## 9. Figma is a live reference, not a one-time input Figma stays open throughout the build. You're using it for five things, and only the first is "what does this look like": 1. **Build reference** — layout, spacing, states 2. **Validate the build against the design** — after you build, compare 3. **Spot missing tokens** — a Figma value with no token behind it 4. **Spot missing design definitions** — a state, variant or breakpoint that was never designed 5. **Catch discrepancies** between design and implementation ### When Figma and the tokens disagree **Do not silently pick one.** Both outcomes are findings: | Situation | What to do | |---|---| | Figma value has no token | Raise with design. Don't hardcode; don't invent a token | | Token exists but Figma shows something else | Raise it — one of them is stale | | A state/variant isn't designed | Raise before building. Don't invent it | | Figma contradicts a confirmed PRD | **Stop.** Cite the doc, section and requirement ID, and ask | Two live examples of why this matters: - The Figma file currently references **`FONTSPRING DEMO - Futura Round Medium`** — a trial font with a reduced character set — while the build ships the licensed Futura Round. Spacing measured off those layers may not match what renders. - **`Neue Haas Grotesk Text Std`** appears in Figma but exists nowhere in the design tokens. Neither is something a FED should resolve alone. Both are exactly what "surface gaps that need resolving" means. --- ## 10. Testing Three layers. **Pick the cheapest one that proves the behaviour — don't duplicate across layers.** | Layer | Tool | Covers | File | |---|---|---|---| | Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms | `*.test.ts` co-located | | Interaction | Storybook `play` | Clicks, form fills, focus, disclosure | in `*.stories.tsx` | | E2E | Playwright | Full journeys, multi-region, integration boundaries | `e2e/tests/zimm/` | **Write a test where failure would be non-obvious or costly to debug:** ✅ Data mapping (Contentful → props, locale/currency transforms, SFCC payload → view model) · integration boundaries · complex state (cart mutations, consent, multi-step flows) · pure logic that would break invisibly in a refactor ❌ Re-exports and one-line passthroughs · visual snapshots · the framework itself (that React renders, that Chakra applies styles) E2E specs are **gherkin-first**: a `.feature` file goes to Lead QA in plain English, and no Playwright is written until it's signed off. Use `/qa-generate`. ```bash npm test # Vitest npx tsc --noEmit # types npm run lint # ESLint ``` --- ## 11. Before you open the PR ```bash /code-quality # audit the diff /pr-checklist # generate the description + checklist ``` Then a local CodeRabbit review — **required, not optional**: ```bash cr review --light --base develop ``` If the CLI isn't authenticated: `coderabbit auth status`, then `coderabbit auth login --api-key "$CODERABBIT_API_KEY"` (`npm run env -- init` pulls the shared key). Findings are advisory — use judgement on fix-now vs let-the-PR-review-catch-it — but the review has to actually run. ### Self-check - [ ] `npx tsc --noEmit` clean - [ ] `npm test` passes - [ ] `npm run lint` clean **for the files I touched** - [ ] No hardcoded hex or px in Chakra props or `.scss` - [ ] `textStyle` used, not raw `fontSize` - [ ] Storybook story exists and is in the right category - [ ] Test where logic-heavy - [ ] Accessibility list from §7 walked, not assumed - [ ] Empty/absent state handled for every optional prop - [ ] Copy-first `console.log` markers removed - [ ] No new MSW handlers in a production path - [ ] Reused what existed, or can justify why not - [ ] Only one protection tier touched ### After CodeRabbit reviews the PR **Reply in-thread to every finding — fixed or not.** CodeRabbit learns from PR conversation, so silence teaches it nothing and a good explanation teaches it to stop flagging a non-issue. - Fixed → short reply confirming it, referencing the commit - Not fixing because it conflicts with a repo rule → say which rule or doc, so it learns the pattern A fix commit with no reply doesn't count. Never silently dismiss. --- ## 12. **`/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Desktop/fed-manual.md`** — 14 sections, saved next to the playbook.

## How it's pitched

The playbook is lead-facing — governance, refinement, estimation, escalation. This is the mirror: what a FED opens when they've picked up a story and are about to write code. Same underlying facts, but sequenced as *do this, then this*, and every rule stated as an instruction rather than a policy.

Structure follows the actual flow of the work: before you code → find what exists → Copy-first → build → apply design → a11y → Storybook → Figma → test → PR.

## The synthesis worth flagging

Your notes framed static-first as a pragmatic response to missing dependencies. **It's already the repo's mandated architecture** — `components.md` requires every component under `overrides/app/components/` to receive data as props, with fetching confined to `pages/`.

I made that the spine of §1. It reframes static-first from "temporary compromise we'll unwind" to "follow the existing rule and you get it for free" — which is both more accurate and much easier to get a team to actually do. Nobody unwinds it later because there's nothing to unwind.

## What I added that wasn't in either source

- **§5 — the `fontSize`/`textStyle` collision.** The single highest-consequence gotcha in the new token set: four Zimmermann keys collide with Chakra defaults used at ~199 base call sites. A FED who writes `fontSize="md"` gets 16px instead of 24px, concludes the theme is broken, and "fixes" it by registering the scale — silently restyling the whole site. Given the tokens land as the build starts, this needed to be prominent and blunt.
- **§5 — hold off on `.zimm-*` classes** until the variable-injection gap is closed, with the reason. Otherwise someone copies the pattern out of `button.ts` and it breaks in Storybook.
- **§9 — the Figma font problem as a worked example.** The demo-font and Neue Haas findings from earlier make "surface gaps rather than absorb them" concrete instead of abstract.
- **§13 — the knowledge-sharing expectation** stated as a working norm with the reason, not as an aspiration.

## Two things to decide

**Where it lives.** It's on Desktop, not in the repo — the current branch is the design-tokens work and dropping an unrelated doc into that PR would muddy it. If you want it in `.docs/`, that's its own branch. Say the word.

**The token assumption.** The manual states up front that it assumes the foundations branch has landed. If that branch stalls, §5 describes a target rather than reality — worth a re-read at merge time.

One caveat on accuracy: the ast-grep and semgrep rule names in §7 and §11 came from your playbook rather than from me reading `.coderabbit/` and `semgrep.yml` directly. Everything else — conventions, tiers, squad boundaries, paths, commands, skills, the token details — I verified against the codebase in this session. Worth a spot-check on those rule names before you circulate it.

# FED Build Approach — Walkthrough Script

**~10 min · 8 beats · speaker notes**
Have open: `.claude/registry/components.md` · Storybook → Foundation · [fed-manual.md](./fed-manual.md)

---

## 0 · Frame — 30s

> "We're building this by hand. No Figma-to-React generation.
>
> That puts three things on us that a generator would have owned: **finding what already exists**,
> **applying tokens properly instead of eyeballing hex off a Figma layer**, and **catching drift
> between design and build** — reporting it, not absorbing it.
>
> That's basically the whole talk. Here's the shape of it."

---

## 1 · The four steps — 1 min

*Put this on screen.*

```
1. Does it already exist in PWA Kit?
2. Use as-is / override / build custom?
3. Execute the swap, override or build.
4. Apply the design styles.
```

> "Step 1 comes before everything, deliberately. Styling is step **four**, not step one — that's
> the part that usually gets done first and it's why things get built twice."

---

## 2 · Check the registry — 2 min  ⟵ **show it**

*Open `.claude/registry/components.md`. Point at Origin · Tier · Squad · Consumers.*

> "This is generated automatically, it's always current, and it's the first thing you open.
>
> Real example: a story lands saying 'build Add to Bag, cart API integration in scope.' The base
> `product-view` component **already calls `addToCart`** — button, label, modal, bundles, the lot.
> That story isn't a build, it's an extend.
>
> Same for size selector — that's `swatch-group`. Quantity — `quantity-picker`. Variant
> resolution — three existing hooks.
>
> Assume it exists. Prove it doesn't before you build."

**The ladder:** PWA Kit base → existing shared component → existing pattern → new build *(justify out loud)*

---

## 3 · The Copy-first tax — 1.5 min

> "One thing to watch in that Origin column. `Base` means it exists in the package but is **not in
> `overrides/` yet** — and there's a cost before you write a single line of your own."

```
copy → convert to TS → tsc --noEmit → add a console marker → STOP
   → a human confirms the override is rendering → then build
```

> "It's serialised and it's human-gated. This is the number one reason a story looks small and
> isn't.
>
> The first story against a given component pays it. Every one after that is cheap. **So tell me at
> refinement, not halfway through the sprint** — it either goes in the estimate or it gets split
> into an enabler."

---

## 4 · Static-first — 1.5 min

> "Contentful's on a demo space, SFCC is a sandbox, Global-e and Adyen haven't started. We are not
> waiting for any of it.
>
> Build the UI properly now. Data arrives as **props**. Fetching lives in `pages/`, never in your
> component.
>
> And this is the bit I want to land: **that's not a temporary workaround.** It's already the rule
> in `components.md` — components take props, containers fetch. Follow the rule you already have
> and static-first costs you nothing. When Contentful goes live, the wiring happens above you and
> your component doesn't change."

> "One thing that will bite: **handle the empty state now.** CMS fields are optional far more often
> than the designs suggest, and the Contentful sync is additive-only — it cannot delete a field
> once it's published. A component that breaks with no `ctaLabel` is a bug we ship."

---

## 5 · Design tokens — 2 min  ⟵ **show Storybook → Foundation**

> "The foundations are landing on develop now — colour, type, spacing, motion, the real Futura
> Round. Browse them here rather than reading the TypeScript.
>
> One trap, and it will catch every one of you once."

*On screen:*

```tsx
<Text textStyle="body1">   ✅
<Text fontSize="md">       ❌
```

| key | Chakra | Zimmermann |
|---|---|---|
| `md` | 16px | **24px** |
| `xs` | 12px | **16px** |

> "Four keys collide, and Chakra's version is used at about **199 places** in the base app. Write
> `fontSize="md"`, you get 16 not 24, and it looks like the theme is broken.
>
> It isn't. **Do not fix it by registering our scale** — there's a test that'll stop you, and if you
> got past it you'd restyle the entire site. Use `textStyle`. Always."

> "Colour — semantic names: `text.default`, `background.01`, `action.primary.bgDefault`. Spacing —
> the named scale: `padding="m"`.
>
> And the line I'd tattoo on this: **a Figma value with no token behind it is a finding, not a
> licence to hardcode.** Nothing catches hardcoded hex automatically yet. That one's on us in review."

---

## 6 · Figma stays open — 1 min

> "Figma isn't a one-time input you build from and close. Five jobs: build reference, validate the
> build back against it, spot missing tokens, spot undesigned states, catch discrepancies.
>
> Two live ones so you know this is real: the Figma file is partly on a **Fontspring demo font** —
> reduced character set, different metrics — while we ship the licensed one. And **Neue Haas
> Grotesk** appears in Figma but exists nowhere in our tokens.
>
> If Figma and the tokens disagree, that's a message to me. It's not a judgement call for you to
> make quietly at 5pm."

---

## 7 · Guardrails — 1 min

*Rapid fire.*

> - "Never work on `develop` or `main`. First command every session: `git branch --show-current`."
> - "Check the tier before you touch anything — `/audit-tier`. One tier per change."
> - "`theme/foundation/` is Tier 1, designer-owned. Tokens don't get changed by us."
> - "Four files are absolute, no approver, no exception: `ssr.js`, `config/default.js`,
>   `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js`."
> - "Don't refactor upward. A bug in a component isn't a licence to change the hook it calls."
> - "No commits, pushes or PRs unless someone asks in that moment. Finishing the work isn't the
>   instruction to ship it."

---

## 8 · Close — 30s

> "Last thing, and it's the one I actually care about most: **ask in the channel.** One question at
> a time. Working something out alone that three of us already know is the most expensive habit on a
> team this size — and the questions with obvious answers are the ones worth asking out loud,
> because that's how everyone else learns them too.
>
> Claude's part of the workflow where it fits. It's not a substitute for asking a person when the
> answer is a project decision rather than a technical one."

**Five to remember:**

1. Check the registry before you build.
2. `textStyle`, never `fontSize`.
3. Data as props.
4. A Figma value with no token is a finding.
5. Ask in the channel.

> "Full detail's in the FED manual — you don't need to read it end to end, just know which section
> to jump to. Questions?"

---

### Pause points
After **2** (registry) · after **5** (tokens) · at the close.

### If you're short on time
Cut **6** and **7** to one line each. **2**, **3**, **4** and **5** are the ones that change behaviour.
